video_title: Why would the Warriors want Anthony Davis AND LeBron James? 🤨 | Get Up

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' pursuit of LeBron James and Anthony Davis is limited
quotes.excerpt: This maneuver limits what they can do trade-wise. It also limits potentially what Draymond can resign for.
quotes.quote: The actions were that Draymond Green opted out of his contract, that gives the Warriors flexibility. But I don't think the Warriors think they're getting Anthony Davis. Because they signed Kristaps Porzingis. And this contract, and Porzingis did not play a lot of games last year for anybody, much less for the Warriors, but you've got to have big men to compete in the Western Conference. They had to handle this business. It's a pretty good contract for Porzingis, two and 40, and he gets a player option on the second year. While the Warriors absolutely can still go after LeBron and I believe they intend to do so today when the window opens, I think they're aggressively going to go after him and try to get him into the fold. This maneuver limits what they can do trade-wise. It also limits potentially what Draymond can resign for. They can still make some moves, but they only have about 33-ish million dollars left that they're going to be allowed to spend, and that's got to be split between LeBron and Draymond Green if they're going to put this team together.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' interest in Anthony Davis makes little sense for either team
quotes.excerpt: I don't understand why the Warriors would want to bring in Anthony Davis who wants an extension.
quotes.quote: I didn't understand why the Warriors would want to bring in Anthony Davis who wants an extension. He's owed 120 million over the next two years, and so your extension would be committing massive salary to Anthony Davis when Steph Curry's probably already been riding off into the sunset. I also don't get how it would make sense for the Wizards. Now look, the Wizards have a problem. They just paid Trey Young and they're trying to tell AD, let's just wait and see on your extension, but they took AD in a trade. They took DeAngelo Russell, who's got a six million dollar vacation fund for this season, Jaden Hardy, another six million dollars. So they'd hypothetically take back Jimmy Butler, still have those salaries on the books, 70 million dollars on the books for maybe a draft pick, maybe call it even two picks. How is Wizards management going to look ownership in the eye and say this expense makes sense for us as we're trying to be competitive this year?

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' future with Lakers remains uncertain amid cap constraints
quotes.excerpt: We don't know if LeBron James wants to play basketball this year. That's kind of a big thing.
quotes.quote: Anything's possible when you consider the fact that the Lakers and LeBron have not had contact. Like Windy has said for a number of weeks, we don't know if LeBron James wants to play basketball this year. That's kind of a big thing. Windy also just told us how much money the Warriors have to split between two players. Even if it's not evenly split between LeBron and Draymond Green, the Lakers know exactly what they're up against. Can they present a number that is palatable to LeBron James to make him want to stay, if they want him to stay? That is the key question here.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' financial flexibility is tied to long-term roster upgrades
quotes.excerpt: This is the one swing that the Lakers have using financial flexibility to make long-term roster upgrades.
quotes.quote: An effort, first of all. Like you know what the Warriors can bid, are you willing to put that on the table? And at this point, it's not clear whether the Lakers really want to keep LeBron James. And would LeBron make them better next season? Absolutely. But this is the one swing that the Lakers have using financial flexibility to make long-term roster upgrades around Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves. And look, this is suspicion, not sourcing, but I'm starting to wonder whether the Lakers are hoping LeBron breaks up with them so they don't have to be the ones to break up with him.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers and LeBron James have not made formal moves
quotes.excerpt: As far as I know, the Lakers haven't made a formal offer just as LeBron has not.
quotes.quote: Again, let's focus on actions. As far as I know, and I am not tapping his phone, but as far as I know the Lakers haven't made a formal offer just as LeBron has not actively accepted a meeting request. Those are not the actions of two parties that are trying to get something done. Just because it hasn't happened, doesn't mean it won't happen. It can happen. What I expect to happen today is an action from the Warriors, which is to reach out to LeBron James and make a contract offer and try to talk him into coming to Golden State to finish his career to play alongside Steph Curry, Draymond Green, and the rest of that roster they've got there.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' cap hold limits their ability to build a team
quotes.excerpt: There is a 58 and a half million dollar cap hold that LeBron James has.
quotes.quote: There is a 58 and a half million dollar cap hold that LeBron James has on the Los Angeles Lakers. That means the Lakers will find it very hard to do actual real team building business until that is situated. If they renounce his rights, that frees up everything. But if LeBron is coming back, both sides need to know this so they can both move on with what they're going to do. 58 and a half million dollars.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Luka Doncic is the focal point of Lakers' future
quotes.excerpt: Luka Doncic clearly it appears now is the focal point of the team.
quotes.quote: There's no question about that and this was the year that the Lakers management pointed to in their discussions with Luka Doncic and his camp and said, hey, summer of 26, we'll have cap space, we'll have flexibility. That's the summer that we're going to make significant long-term upgrades. Well, it's the summer of 26, the time is now. They've got to put supporting cast pieces in place right now to deliver on their promise to the guy who's now the face of their franchise.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' roster construction challenges with LeBron James and Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: This is the problem that the Lakers are on two different tracks.
quotes.quote: He's been that way since they traded for him or since rather he fell into their lap. This is the problem that the Lakers are on two different tracks. When LeBron got there, LeBron was the first priority. You wound up getting Anthony Davis, you wound up trading for Russell Westbrook. One thing worked, one thing didn't. Luka comes there, he's younger, he becomes the first priority. That's where things get tricky for the Lakers and LeBron James because neither player lines up with a Lakers timeline cleanly. LeBron is going to be 42 years old. You can't sign on a multi-year contracts while still fulfilling the needs that Luka Doncic has. Wing help as far as defenders, rim help as far as rim runners. Can you do all of those things and treat LeBron James with respect? That's a very fine needle to thread.
